title: Do You Watch for the Game or the Ads?
main_content:
Out of the eight most-watched programs in U.S. television history, only one was not the Super Bowl football game.

The number of people who watched the football game on television has been larger than 100 million every year since 2010.

In the United States, watching the game with friends has become like a holiday.

People who watch the game are not only interested in what happens on the field. The commercials and the halftime show are big draws. This year, the halftime performers are the British band Coldplay and singer Beyonce.

The Super Bowl is a spectacle in the U.S. It is played in a huge sports arena where almost 70,000 fans cheer and make noise.

Media and advertising companies measure how viewers react to the advertising during the game.

Alan Siegel is a writer for USA Today. He says he thinks fans turned their attention to the ads, or commercials, 20 years ago. Some of the games in the 1990s were not very competitive, and the winner seemed to be decided early in the game.

As a result, people started paying more attention to the commercials.

questions.question: What were the Super Bowl games like in the 90s?
options: A. Highly competitive and thrilling until the final whistle.
B. Generally unexciting with predictable outcomes.
C. Filled with memorable halftime shows and iconic moments.
D. Characterized by extensive media coverage and advertising.
questions.answer: B. Generally unexciting with predictable outcomes.

questions.question: Who are the halftime performers this year?
options: A. The Rolling Stones and Taylor Swift.
C. Katy Perry and Bruno Mars.

questions.question: What has watching the Super Bowl with friends become like in the US?
options: A. A casual gathering with little significance.
B. A major cultural event similar to a holiday.
C. An opportunity for sports betting and gambling.
D. A family-oriented tradition focused only on sports.
questions.answer: B. A major cultural event similar to a holiday.
